text: LiberNT: An AI-Fueled Fork Of ReactOS Focused On Windows 11 Compatibility Written by Michael Larabel in Operating Systems on 19 November 2026 at 07:56 AM EST. 31 Comments While the ReactOS project has been enjoying nice conventional progress this year from initial USB 3.0 driver support to improved DirectX support , there is now a new project called LiberNT that is forked from the ReactOS codebase and leveraging AI to quickly iterate on it with a goal of Windows 11 compatibility. Several readers have brought up LiberNT over the past day as a "free NT operating system" focused on Windows 11 compatibility. LiberNT is not only for Intel/AMD x86_64 systems but also ARM64 and even RISC-V 64-bit too. "LiberNT is a free NT operating system. The name says it: liber is Latin for free. It targets Windows® 11 compatibility, with room for freestyle and experimental features. LiberNT brings extensive work on kernel-space components and drivers, aimed at stability and modern hardware, and it focuses on 64-bit platforms: amd64, arm64 and riscv64. Our goal is a system that stays maintainable in the long run: stable, reliable and efficient, running on embedded devices too, and able to support every feature a modern operating system should have." LiberNT can run on bare metal hardware or within VMs. They are transparent about their AI use and in leveraging AI is how they are quickly driving new improvements to this open-source project. The AGENTS documentation permits sources of truth as official Windows SDK and WDK headers, Windows 11 public symbols, and black-box runs on Windows 11 itself. Plus, like ReactOS, leveraging Wine code too. Those curious about this LiberNT project can learn more via GitHub and LiberNT.com . 31 Comments
